The player's background can be a Visualizer that moves with the music, from built-in shaders or ones shared on chroma.pw.
Mod Settings have a Workshop of shaders, audio presets, headphone corrections and fonts to download.
AutoMix blends each song into the next on playlists, albums and radio, beat-matched or as a crossfade.
Animated artwork in the player and on the lock screen, animated album covers, artist logos, line meanings and Vibrations no longer need Plus.
Chroma runs on Spotify 9.1.90 as well as 9.1.78.
A volume slider can sit under the player's controls, for this iPhone or the Connect device playing.
Audio presets have a library in the Workshop, and the effects you set save as a preset of your own.
Thirty-one fonts download from the Workshop and set the type of the whole app.
The player's accent colour can follow the cover of the song playing.
Home's shortcuts sit on glass tinted by their covers, and Home scrolls more smoothly.
Older iPhones can pick a lighter voice model for Sing, and Sing can ignore memory warnings.
An Appearance option swaps Spotify's circled tick for a plain checkmark in the accent colour.
Lyrics and the next song's animated artwork load ahead of time, and Chroma does less work in the background.
Sing has its own category, goes up to vocals only, keeps going on a hot iPhone, and its voice can follow your head with AirPods.
Lyrics translate into any language, from Musixmatch's community or, with a Gemini key of your own, on a tap.
The Lyrics page opens on a live preview with presets, the sung word glows, and a held word's letters rise in a wave.
Turning the phone puts the lyrics on a screen of their own beside the cover, and a scroll through them hides the player's controls.
With AirPods in, a double nod likes the song and a shake of the head skips it, learned from how you move.
Every song can animate on the lock screen, and full-screen lyrics are a choice beside the artwork.
The Live Activity carries the cover's colours and a progress bar, translates the lyrics, and reaches Apple Watch, CarPlay and StandBy.
The redesign's Player page leads with a live preview of the player, and Switch to video can be hidden.
Audio effects get presets, and AutoEq corrections for your headphones.
Top songs, artists and albums are counted on this iPhone, and Spotify's own export can be imported.
Local files get lyrics in the redesigned player, and Edit Info changes their title, artist, album and cover.
Holding either side of the cover plays faster until the finger lifts.
Music Haptics keep going in the background and on the lock screen.
A new Appearance page sets one font for the whole app, the accent colour, now with Apple Music's red, and the app icon.
The redesign's Tab bar page shows the bar it makes, and Spotify's own tabs take a name and icon of your own.
Albums and Artists have their own settings, album track lists can hide the artists, and artist pages show Apple Music's logo.
Mod Settings take the system Settings' look with an Account page, and a setting that waits on a switch stays greyed out under it.

You translate song lyrics for a lyrics screen that shows each translated line under the original line while the song plays.
The user message is JSON: the target language, and the song's lines in the order they are sung, each with a number n. A line sung several times appears once.
Answer with JSON {"lines":[{"n":1,"text":"..."}]}: exactly one entry for every input line, with its n, in the same order.

- Read the whole song first, then translate each line the way a fluent native speaker of the target language would say it: natural and idiomatic, true to the meaning, tone and register. Translate the sense, not word for word; render idioms, slang and wordplay by what they mean.
- Keep each line's content in its own line. Never merge, split, skip or reorder lines. Keep pronouns, gender, tense and recurring images consistent across the song.
- Keep a line about as short as the original. Rhyme and meter are not needed.
- Keep profanity, sexual content, violence and drug references at the same strength. Do not soften, censor or comment.
- Leave names, places, brands and titles as they are, and vocal sounds such as oh, yeah, la la la or na na.
- Text in parentheses is a backing vocal: translate it and keep the parentheses.
- A line already in the target language stays as it is. In a line mixing languages, translate the parts that are not in the target language.
- Write only the translation: no quotes, notes, romanization or original text.
